hero.title: 10 Best Street Food in Almaty
hero.dek: The best street food in Almaty — curated from local reviews, travel blogs, and food communities. Samsa, shashlik, laghman, manty, and more. Interactive map included.

intro.answerFirst: Almaty isn't just Kazakhstan's largest city — it's the culinary crossroads of Central Asia. The former capital sits at the intersection of Kazakh nomadic traditions, Silk Road trading routes, and Soviet-era influences, creating a street food scene unlike anywhere else.
body: The city's signature street foods reflect this heritage: samsa (flaky meat pastries baked in clay tandoor ovens), shashlik (marinated meat skewers grilled over charcoal), laghman (hand-pulled noodles in savory broth brought by Uyghur immigrants), and manty (steamed dumplings with spiced lamb). Add in baursak (puffy fried dough), kurt (portable dried cheese balls), and kumis (fermented mare's milk), and you have a cuisine built for nomads and travelers.

The Green Bazaar, operating since 1875, remains the beating heart of Almaty's food culture — a two-story labyrinth of spices, dried fruits, fresh meats, and food stalls serving everything from simple samsa to elaborate plov feasts. Beyond the bazaar, dedicated shashlik houses, Dungan noodle shops, and modern Kazakh restaurants offer deeper dives into specific cuisines.
We analyzed dozens of travel blogs, food guides, and local recommendations from the Almaty food community and r/Kazakhstan to build this guide.
intro.methodology: We analyzed travel blogs, food guides, TripAdvisor reviews, and local recommendations from the Almaty food community and r/Kazakhstan. Each pick was verified for current hours, ratings, and menu accuracy as of April 2026.

picks.name: Green Bazaar (Zelyony Bazaar)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Every Almaty food guide starts here. The market has operated since 1875 and remains the city's culinary heart.
picks.whatToOrder: Fresh samsa from any tandoor, laghman from the upstairs food court, kurt samples from dried goods vendors.
picks.insiderTip: First-time visitors wanting to sample everything Kazakh in one place
picks.bestFor: First-time visitors wanting to sample everything Kazakh in one place
picks.limitations: Can be crowded · Quality varies by stall · Cash preferred

redditQuotes.quote: This is where locals actually shop. The upstairs food court has incredibly cheap and authentic Kazakh food.

picks.name: Shashlik Dvor
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Consistently rated as Almaty's best shashlik. The smoky, perfectly charred meat and lively outdoor seating make it unmissable.
picks.whatToOrder: Lamb shashlik is the signature — order with fresh bread, grilled vegetables, and tangy adjika sauce.
picks.insiderTip: Shashlik purists wanting the best grilled meats in Almaty
picks.bestFor: Shashlik purists wanting the best grilled meats in Almaty
picks.limitations: Limited menu beyond shashlik · Gets smoky · Casual setting

picks.name: Navat
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Featured on every Almaty food tour. The Central Asian-style decor and consistently excellent food make it a must-visit.
picks.whatToOrder: The signature plov (rice pilaf with lamb), manty (steamed dumplings), and Uzbek bread fresh from the tandoor.
picks.insiderTip: Travelers wanting authentic Central Asian food in a comfortable setting
picks.bestFor: Travelers wanting authentic Central Asian food in a comfortable setting
picks.limitations: More restaurant than street food · Higher prices than stalls

picks.name: Qaimaq
picks.neighborhood: Abay Ave 46a, Bostandyk District (near Baikonur Metro)
picks.address: Abay Ave 46a, Bostandyk District (near Baikonur Metro)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Consistently rated as one of the best Kazakh restaurants in Almaty. If you want to try beshbarmak or kazy, this is the place.
picks.whatToOrder: Beshbarmak (boiled horse or lamb with noodles) is essential. Try kumis (fermented mare's milk) if you're adventurous.
picks.insiderTip: Experiencing authentic Kazakh nomadic cuisine done right
picks.bestFor: Experiencing authentic Kazakh nomadic cuisine done right
picks.limitations: Adventurous menu (horse meat) · Not for vegetarians

picks.name: Dungan House
picks.whyItMadeTheList: The laghman here is legendary — the noodles are hand-pulled to order, and the broth is one of the most aromatic in the city.
picks.whatToOrder: Kattama laghman (soup style) or tsomyan laghman (stir-fried). Try ganfan (rice with meat and vegetables) as a side.
picks.insiderTip: Laghman lovers seeking the most authentic hand-pulled noodles in Almaty
picks.bestFor: Laghman lovers seeking the most authentic hand-pulled noodles in Almaty
picks.limitations: Simple setting · Limited English · Cash preferred

picks.name: Baursak City
picks.neighborhood: Muratbayeva St / Bogenbay Batyr, Almaly District
picks.address: Muratbayeva St / Bogenbay Batyr, Almaly District
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Baursak is central to Kazakh hospitality — served at every celebration and gathering. This spot elevates it to an art form.
picks.whatToOrder: Fresh baursak with honey, served alongside traditional Kazakh tea with milk. Try the kurt (dried cheese) as well.
picks.insiderTip: Experiencing Kazakh tea culture and traditional snacks
picks.bestFor: Experiencing Kazakh tea culture and traditional snacks

picks.name: Tarkhun
picks.whyItMadeTheList: One of the most versatile Central Asian restaurants in Almaty. Perfect when your group can't agree on one cuisine.
picks.whatToOrder: Try the plov alongside Georgian khachapuri (cheese bread) for a taste of the Silk Road's culinary diversity.
picks.insiderTip: Groups wanting variety — traditional and fusion dishes on one menu
picks.bestFor: Groups wanting variety — traditional and fusion dishes on one menu
picks.limitations: Jack of all trades · Less specialized than focused spots

picks.name: Venezia
picks.neighborhood: Kairbekov St 72, Medeu District (by Malaya Almatinka River)
picks.address: Kairbekov St 72, Medeu District (by Malaya Almatinka River)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: The riverside setting elevates the shashlik experience. Some locals consider this the best shashlik in Almaty.
picks.whatToOrder: Mixed shashlik platter with lamb, beef, and chicken. The riverside location calls for cold beer.

picks.name: Gakku
picks.whyItMadeTheList: The yurt setting and focus on nomadic traditions make this more than a restaurant — it's a window into Kazakh heritage.
picks.whatToOrder: Beshbarmak prepared in the traditional style. Ask about kazy (horse sausage) and kumis (fermented mare's milk).
picks.insiderTip: Immersive Kazakh cultural dining in a yurt-style setting
picks.bestFor: Immersive Kazakh cultural dining in a yurt-style setting
picks.limitations: Located outside central Almaty · Focused menu

picks.name: Tyubeteika
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Consistently good Uzbek-style food in a convenient location. Great for a reliable Central Asian meal.
picks.whatToOrder: The Uzbek plov is the specialty — rice cooked with lamb, carrots, and spices. Don't skip the fresh non bread.
picks.insiderTip: Convenient Central Asian food on Almaty's main avenue

faq.question: What is the most popular street food in Almaty?
faq.answer: Samsa is arguably the most popular street food in Almaty — savory pastries filled with meat, onions, and spices, baked in a traditional tandoor oven. You'll find samsa stands on nearly every corner, and they're cheap, satisfying, and perfect for eating on the go.

faq.question: Where is the best place to try street food in Almaty?
faq.answer: The Green Bazaar (Zelyony Bazaar) is the ultimate destination for street food in Almaty. This historic market dating back to 1875 has hundreds of food stalls offering samsa, laghman, shashlik, plov, and traditional Kazakh snacks.

faq.question: How much does street food cost in Almaty?
faq.answer: Street food in Almaty is very affordable. Expect to pay ₸300-500 for samsa, ₸800-1500 for laghman, ₸1000-2000 for shashlik skewers. A full street food meal typically costs ₸1500-3000 ($3.30-6.60).

faq.question: What is laghman and where can I find the best in Almaty?
faq.answer: Laghman is a Central Asian noodle dish featuring hand-pulled noodles in a savory broth with meat and vegetables. For the best laghman, try Dungan House for authentic Uyghur-style preparation, or the food stalls at Green Bazaar.

faq.question: Is street food safe to eat in Almaty?
faq.answer: Yes, street food in Almaty is generally safe. Stick to busy stalls with high turnover. Samsa fresh from the tandoor and shashlik straight off the grill are always safe bets.

faq.question: What is beshbarmak and can I find it as street food?
faq.answer: Beshbarmak is Kazakhstan's national dish — boiled meat served over flat noodles with onion sauce. While typically a sit-down dish, you can find simplified versions at Green Bazaar. For the authentic experience, visit Qaimaq or Gakku restaurant.

faq.question: What are the best vegetarian street food options in Almaty?
faq.answer: While Kazakh cuisine is meat-heavy, vegetarians can enjoy kartoshka samsa (potato samsa), non bread, baursak (fried dough), kurt (dried cheese balls), and vegetable laghman.

faq.question: When is the best time to eat street food in Almaty?
faq.answer: For the freshest street food, visit markets like Green Bazaar in the morning (8-11am). Shashlik spots are best in the evening when the grills are fired up. Summer months (June-August) offer the best outdoor dining experience.
